title: Half-Smoke, All The Way
subject: a lunchtime food-truck line on a DC sidewalk where the cook calls out orders in rhythm
caption: DC go-go in the classic live-band pocket. Congas and timbales driving the syncopated go-go swing beat with a cowbell on top; a tight kick and snare pocket; a busy funk bass; short brass horn section blasts on the hits; keyboard organ stabs. Live and sweaty, percussion forward, the crowd answers mixed loud, no gaps between sections. Male lead talker, a raspy baritone running call-and-response with a crowd that shouts back every line, chanting the chorus. 96 BPM, E minor. Rowdy, hungry and grinning. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no drum machine, no EDM drop, no rap verse over a beat track.
lyrics:
[Intro - congas, cowbell and timbales]

[Verse 1]
Twelve-oh-two on Fourteenth Street, the line's around the corner
Big Tony in the window got the tongs up like a drumstick
He don't write nothing down, he just calls it on the beat
Half-smoke, chili, onions, now who's next, who's next

[Pre-Chorus]
If you're hungry say yeah
Yeah
If you're late for work say yeah
Yeah

[Chorus]
Half-smoke, all the way
Big Tony, what you say
Mustard on the left side, napkin in the bag
Half-smoke, all the way

[Verse 2]
Lady from the bank wants it no onion, Tony shakes his head
Man in the suit tryna pay with his phone, Tony points at the sign
Cash only since 1998, he hollers it in time
Whole line stomping on the sidewalk like a show

[Chorus - crowd louder]
Half-smoke, all the way
Big Tony, what you say
Cash in the bucket and the cheese on top
Half-smoke, and the beat don't stop

[Outro - horns and percussion]
Tony says come back tomorrow
Same time, same song
